title: dispatch() rejects payloads missing targetUserId, organizationId, or message
description: notification.service.js dispatch() validates the three required fields before touching Mongo; on a miss it logs a warning and returns null instead of throwing.
preconditions: notificationService.dispatch is callable directly in a unit test context (Mongo connection mocked or test DB)
steps: Call dispatch({ targetUserId: 'u1', organizationId: 'org1' }) with message omitted
Call dispatch({ organizationId: 'org1', message: 'hi' }) with targetUserId omitted
Call dispatch({ targetUserId: 'u1', message: 'hi' }) with organizationId omitted
expectedResult: All three calls return null, no Notification document is created, and a '[NotificationService] dispatch called with missing required fields' warning is logged for each.

title: dispatch() never throws — internal errors are caught and swallowed
description: The entire dispatch() body is wrapped in try/catch; a downstream failure (e.g. Notification.create rejecting on a bad ObjectId string) must log via logger.error and return null, never propagate to the caller. This guarantees a broken notification path can never fail the business action that triggered it (e.g. an audit assignment).
preconditions: Mongoose write can be forced to reject (e.g. invalid organizationId type or DB connection dropped)
steps: Call dispatch() with a malformed organizationId that fails mongoose.Types.ObjectId() casting inside the try block, or stub Notification.create to reject
Await the call from the caller's perspective
expectedResult: The promise resolves to null (never rejects), and '[NotificationService] dispatch failed' is logged at error level with the underlying error.

title: dispatch() merges legacy meta and new metadata into both fields for backward/forward compatibility
description: mergedMeta = { ...meta, ...metadata, projectId } is written to BOTH doc.meta and doc.metadata so old consumers reading meta and new consumers reading metadata see the same data.
steps: Call dispatch() with meta={ foo: 1 } and metadata={ bar: 2 } and projectId='p1'
expectedResult: doc.meta and doc.metadata are both equal to { foo: 1, bar: 2, projectId: 'p1' } (metadata keys win on conflict since they are spread last).

title: getMyNotifications with surface='popup' restricts to unread, urgent/actionable types, max 5
description: getMyNotifications applies filter.isRead=false plus an $or of priority in [high,critical] OR notificationType in a fixed actionable list, and clamps effectiveLimit to min(5, limit) only for the popup surface.
preconditions: A user has 8 unread notifications: 3 low-priority 'general', 5 mixed high-priority/actionable types
expectedResult: Result contains at most 5 notifications, all isRead=false, and each either has priority in ['high','critical'] or notificationType in the actionable list (task_assigned, task_reassigned, task_overdue, review_requested, audit_invitation, escalation_required). The 3 low-priority 'general' unread items are excluded.

title: getMyNotifications backfills metadata from legacy meta for old documents
description: The mapping step in getMyNotifications sets metadata = (doc.metadata non-empty) ? doc.metadata : (doc.meta || {}) so pre-migration documents that only ever wrote to `meta` still return a populated `metadata` field to API consumers.
preconditions: A Notification document exists with meta={ module: 'vendor' } and metadata={} (empty object, simulating a pre-migration write)
steps: Call getMyNotifications for the user owning that document
expectedResult: The returned notification's metadata field equals { module: 'vendor' }, not an empty object.

title: getUnreadCount scopes strictly to targetUserId + organizationId
preconditions: User A (org X) has 3 unread notifications; a different user in the same org has 2 unread; a user with the same _id string in a different org has 1 unread
expectedResult: Returns exactly 3 — counts from the other org-scoped user and the cross-org same-id user are not included.

title: markRead only updates a notification owned by the calling user
description: markRead's findOneAndUpdate filter is { _id, targetUserId: String(userId) } — a valid notificationId that belongs to a different targetUserId must not match and returns null (route layer turns this into 404).
expectedResult: Returns null; N.isRead remains false and N.readAt remains unset in the database.

title: TTL index only expires notifications that are read, unread notifications never auto-delete
description: notification.model.js defines { createdAt: 1 } with expireAfterSeconds: 90*24*60*60 and partialFilterExpression: { isRead: true }. MongoDB's TTL monitor only considers documents matching the partial filter, so isRead=false documents are exempt regardless of age.
preconditions: Direct access to a test MongoDB instance to inspect index definitions (or a long-running TTL simulation environment)
steps: Run db.notifications.getIndexes() against the notifications collection
Locate the createdAt_1 index and inspect its expireAfterSeconds and partialFilterExpression
expectedResult: expireAfterSeconds = 7776000 (90 days) and partialFilterExpression = { isRead: true }; confirms unread notifications are excluded from TTL cleanup and cannot silently disappear from a user's inbox before they are read.

title: internalAuth returns 503 when INTERNAL_API_TOKEN/INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN is unset, 401 on a timing-safe mismatch
description: notification-internal.routes.js reads INTERNAL_TOKEN once at module load. If empty, every request 503s with 'Internal endpoint not configured' before ever reaching crypto.timingSafeEqual. Otherwise it length-checks then timing-safe-compares the header value.
preconditions: Two test runs: one with INTERNAL_API_TOKEN unset, one with it set to a known value
steps: With the env var unset, POST /api/internal/notifications with any X-Internal-Token header
With the env var set, POST /api/internal/notifications with a header of a different length than the configured token
With the env var set, POST /api/internal/notifications with a header of the correct length but wrong bytes
expectedResult: Step 1 returns 503 'Internal endpoint not configured'. Steps 2 and 3 both return 401 'Unauthorized: invalid internal token' without ever leaking timing differences between a length mismatch and a content mismatch.
